messages:
maya (PM): Quick sync — we need a final decision on priorities for the SDK starter kits, quickstarts, and two sample apps for the next roadmap slice. Customer asks stack: TypeScript-first SDK, a small-footprint embedding + search sample, and a multi-model routing example. Can we lock by EOW?

jonah (DevEx Lead): +1 on TypeScript-first. My proposal: prioritize TS SDK + one full sample (vector search + minimal UI) and a second lightweight routing demo. Postpone heavy plugin/tool-calling sample to next quarter.

lei (Eng): Implementation note — TS SDK work looks fine but the routing demo needs changes to the smart routing policy API (minor). We can do TS SDK + vector sample in 2 sprints if we drop the plugin sample. Need 1 backend eng + 1 infra for caching/kv work.

axel (Docs): Docs impact: we'll need a migration guide for existing Python-first customers, plus a quickstart README and a reference snippet. Suggest a single canonical quickstart that shows: auth, run, embed, and query. I can draft the README and examples if scope is stable.

maya (PM): Proposed minimal launch criteria (must-haves):
- time-to-first-request <= 10m on a fresh repo (cloned + setup)
- sample app deploy script (one-liner) works in default dev env
- CI smoke tests for SDK basic flows (init, generate, embed) pass
- docs quickstart + one end-to-end tutorial published
- at least one external beta customer committed to try it
If any of the above fails, we ship as "beta" with clear caveats and follow-up plan.

tasha (Growth): For beta we'll need a short onboarding funnel: walkthrough video (2-3m), copy for in-app banners, and an opt-in feedback form. I can run the campaign and measure "time-to-first-request" drop. Also recommend we capture "first 5 API calls" metric.

jonah (DevEx Lead): Scope trade-offs proposal:
- MVP (ship this quarter): TypeScript SDK + vector-search sample app + docs quickstart + deploy script + CI smoke tests
- Stretch: multi-model routing demo (lightweight), sample analytics dashboard, migration guide expanded for Python
- Defer: plugin/tool-calling sample, enterprise-only dedicated samples
This keeps dev cost to roughly 3 sprints.

lei (Eng): Agree but need clarity on runtime compatibility: which quantized kernels / model variants must be supported by SDK examples? If we require Q4 quantization profiles, that's additional work. Can we mark the vector-search sample as "optimized for recommended quant profiles" and include fallback?

axel (Docs): Draft quickstart snippet for README (will expand):
```
# Install
npm install @redwood-inference/sdk

# Quickstart
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })

const r = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd/claude-lite', prompt: 'Summarize this doc' })
console.log(r.text)
```
Include a section: "If you see errors about kernel compatibility -> try model: rwd/compat-small"

ci-bot: New RFC created: devex/starterkits-2026 — reviewers: @jonah @axel @lei @maya

maya (PM): Action items:
- jonah: draft engineering plan & slot allocation by Tue EOD (include infra needs)
- lei: list runtime compatibility constraints and minimal supported model variants by Wed
- axel: initial quickstart draft + sample README by Thu
- tasha: beta outreach playbook + metrics to capture by Thu
- maya: compile launch criteria doc and risk register, decide go/no-go Friday

jonah (DevEx Lead): I’ll start the ticket and sync with infra. If we get 2 devs for the first sprint, we can hit MVP scope.

lei (Eng): Acknowledged. I’ll add the quant/profile details to the ticket and list what needs infra changes.

axel (Docs): Will open PR for docs draft and tag reviewers.

maya (PM): Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for scope decisions. I'll update the RFC once the inputs land. :+1:
